lines: Three-month history of palpitations, heat intolerance, unintentional weight loss despite increased appetite, frequent bowel movements, and insomnia.
She also reports experiencing frequent bowel movements and difficulty sleeping.
Her mother has an autoimmune thyroid condition
Alcohol: None; denies alcohol use during pregnancy.
Occupation: High school physical education teacher.
On examination, she appears anxious and has a fine tremor of her outstretched hands. her skin is warm and moist.
You note a diffuse, non-tender goiter without nodularity.
Her TSH level is <0.01 IU/mL (normal: 0.4-4.0 IU/mL), free T4 is 3 ng/dL (normal: 0.9-1.7 ng/dL), and total T3 is 300 ng/dL (normal: 80-180 ng/dL).

encounters.cc: Presents for routine fetal anatomy scan at 20 weeks gestation.

lines: Presents for routine fetal anatomy scan at 20 weeks gestation.

The patient is a 31-year-old female with a history of Graves disease initially diagnosed in January 2020 and chronic hepatitis B infection who returns for a routine fetal anatomy scan at 20 weeks gestation.
She has been on antithyroid therapy for the past 3 years.
At the time of confirming her pregnancy, she was still taking methimazole, which she had been using consistently for several months.
Her medication was later switched to propylthiouracil at her first prenatal visit, which occurred around 12 weeks gestation.
She reports no other medication use, no infections, and no substance use.
She asks if her early pregnancy medication could have affected the baby.
Alcohol: None; denies alcohol use during pregnancy.
Occupation: High school physical education teacher.
The ultrasound reveals a live, singleton fetus with normal growth parameters and normal fluid volume.

encounters.cc: Routine prenatal visit to discuss appropriate weight gain and caloric intake during pregnancy.

lines: Routine prenatal visit to discuss appropriate weight gain and caloric intake during pregnancy.
The patient returns for routine prenatal follow-up in the context of established Graves disease and a prior anatomy scan demonstrating aplasia cutis congenita.
She has a normal prepregnancy BMI of 22 and has gained 10 kg (22 lb) since the beginning of her pregnancy.
She reports following a balanced diet and taking her prenatal vitamins regularly.
She inquires about the appropriate amount of weight gain and caloric intake for the remainder of her pregnancy.
Alcohol: None; denies alcohol use during pregnancy.
Occupation: High school physical education teacher.
Her physical examination is within normal limits.
Her obstetric examination is consistent with a 24-week gestation, and fetal heart tones are normal.

encounters.cc: Routine prenatal visit to inquire about safety of continuing basketball coaching activities.

lines: Routine prenatal visit to inquire about safety of continuing basketball coaching activities.
The patient with Graves disease, chronic hepatitis B, and migraine returns for second-trimester prenatal care following August and June visits.
She has had an uncomplicated pregnancy thus far.
She expresses a desire to continue participating in the school's sports program, which includes coaching basketball.
She inquires about the safety of her involvement in the program.
She has no known drug allergies
She is a high school physical education teacher and is accustomed to an active lifestyle.
Her vital signs are within normal limits
Her obstetric examination is consistent with a 16-week gestation, and fetal heart tones are normal.
She has no contraindications to exercise based on her medical and obstetric history.

encounters.cc: Routine prenatal visit with reports of increased shortness of breath when climbing stairs and mild ankle swelling by end of day.

lines: Routine prenatal visit with reports of increased shortness of breath when climbing stairs and mild ankle swelling by end of day.

With Graves disease and chronic hepatitis B, she reports feeling generally well but has noticed increased shortness of breath when climbing stairs and mild swelling in her ankles by the end of the day.
Her obstetric history is significant for one previous full-term normal vaginal delivery with no complications.
Alcohol: None; denies alcohol use during pregnancy.
Occupation: High school physical education teacher.
On examination, her blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute
Cardiac examination reveals a grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard best at the left sternal border that decreases in intensity when she sits up from a supine position.
Lung fields are clear to auscultation.
There is mild pitting edema in both ankles.

encounters.cc: Twenty-four-hour history of throbbing bitemporal headache accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light.

lines: Twenty-four-hour history of throbbing bitemporal headache accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light.
The patient with Graves returns for obstetrics follow-up.
She reports headache is accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light.
She has a history of migraines, which have increased in frequency since becoming pregnant.
Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable.
Alcohol: None; denies alcohol use during pregnancy.
Occupation: High school physical education teacher.
She denies any recent head trauma, fever, neck stiffness, or visual changes.
Her blood pressure is 122/78 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, and temperature is 98.6°F (37°C).
Physical examination is unremarkable, with no signs of focal neurological deficits.
Given her pregnancy and migraine history, you consider appropriate treatment options for her acute symptoms.

encounters.cc: Routine prenatal visit with no specific complaints.

lines: Routine prenatal visit with no specific complaints.
Patient with Graves disease and hepatitis B returns for routine prenatal care.
She has no complaints and has had an uneventful pregnancy thus far.
Alcohol: None; denies alcohol use during pregnancy.
Occupation: High school physical education teacher.
She denies any history of bruising, bleeding, or anemia.
Her blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 82 beats per minute
Physical examination is normal with no petechiae, purpura, or hepatosplenomegaly.
- Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT): 30 seconds (control 25-35 seconds)

encounters.cc: Presents to labor and delivery unit in active labor.

lines: Presents to labor and delivery unit in active labor.
The patient with Graves disease and hepatitis B presents in active labor following care for aplasia cutis congenita and thrombocytopenia.
She has been compliant with her prenatal care and reports no complications during her pregnancy.
Her first child is healthy with no chronic illnesses.
She has no history of drug allergies
Alcohol: None; denies alcohol use during pregnancy.
Occupation: High school physical education teacher.
On examination, her vital signs are stable
, and the fetal heart tracing is reassuring.
Her prenatal labs were significant for positive HBsAg and HBeAg.
She delivers a healthy male infant weighing 3,400 grams via spontaneous vaginal delivery.
The infant's Apgar scores are 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively.
